name: Dice and Cubes — Finding the Opposite Face
whatIsIt: Dice questions show one or more views of the same cube (or die) from different angles, and ask which face is opposite a given face. For a STANDARD die, opposite faces always add to 7. For a die with unknown or non-standard labels, you find opposite faces by comparing two views: any face seen next to a given face in EITHER view can't be its opposite — only the one face never seen next to it in any view is truly opposite.
whyNeeded: This builds 3D spatial visualization from flat 2D pictures — mentally tracking which faces are adjacent versus opposite as a cube rotates is a core spatial-reasoning skill useful in geometry, packaging, and design.
realLifeUses: Reasoning sections of SSC, banking, and railway exams
Understanding cube nets and 3D shape folding in geometry
Packaging and box design (which panels end up opposite each other when folded)

vocabulary.meaning: A regular die (like the ones used in board games) where opposite faces always add up to 7: 1-6, 2-5, 3-4.
A face that touches (shares an edge with) another face — adjacent faces can NEVER be opposite each other.
The face directly across the cube from a given face — the two faces you'd see if you sliced straight through the cube.
A face that appears in the same view (e.g. on top) in two different pictures of the same die.

story.title: Two Photos of One Die
story.text: Ishaan's uncle shows two photos of the same die. In photo 1: top=2, and the visible side faces show 3 and 4. In photo 2, the die has been rolled, but 2 is STILL on top — this time the visible sides show 5 and 6. 'Which face is opposite 2?' asks his uncle. Ishaan lists every face he's seen next to 2 across both photos: 3, 4, 5, 6 — four different faces, none of them opposite. Since a die only has 6 faces, and 1 has never appeared next to 2 in either photo, 1 must be the one directly opposite 2.
story.extractedProblem: Photo 1 of a die: top=2, sides show 3 and 4. Photo 2 (same die, re-rolled): top=2, sides show 5 and 6. The die has faces 1-6. Which face is opposite 2?
story.answerInStory: 1 is opposite 2 — every other face (3,4,5,6) was seen adjacent to 2 across the two photos, leaving only 1 unaccounted for.

visual.caption: Face 2 is on top in both positions. Faces 3, 4, 5 and 6 all appear adjacent to it across the two views — only face 1 is never seen next to 2, so 1 must be opposite it.

teachingGallery.title: Standard die shortcut: opposite faces sum to 7
teachingGallery.note: For an ordinary numbered die (1 through 6), you don't need two views at all — opposite faces always add up to 7. This only works for standard dice, not dice with letters, colors, or unusual numbers.

examples.caption: On a standard die, 3's opposite face is always 4, because 3 + 4 = 7 — no second view needed.

standardMethod.summary: For a STANDARD numbered die, use the sum-to-7 shortcut directly. For any other die (unknown or non-standard labels), find two views sharing one common face; list every face seen adjacent to that common face across both views; the one remaining face never seen adjacent to it is the opposite face.
steps: Check if the die is a standard 1-6 die — if so, opposite faces sum to 7, no further work needed.
Otherwise, find two given views that share one common face (e.g. both show the same number on top).
List every distinct face seen adjacent to that common face across BOTH views.
The one face from the full set that never appears in that adjacent list is the opposite face.

alternateMethods.name: Single-view adjacency elimination
alternateMethods.whenToUse: When only one view is given but you already know several adjacency facts from other clues.
steps: List all faces already confirmed adjacent to the target face from any given information.
A cube has exactly 4 faces adjacent to any given face, and only 1 opposite face.
Once 4 distinct adjacent faces are confirmed, the one remaining face (out of 6 total) must be the opposite.
alternateMethods.example: If faces 2, 3, 5, 6 are all confirmed adjacent to face 1 (on a die with faces 1-6), then face 4 must be opposite face 1.

workedExamples.problem: A standard die shows 3 on top. What face is on the bottom (opposite 3)?
steps: Standard die rule: opposite faces sum to 7.

workedExamples.problem: A die (faces 1-6, non-standard arrangement) is shown in two positions. Position 1: top=2, sides show 3 and 4. Position 2 (same die, re-rolled): top=2, sides show 5 and 6. Which face is opposite 2?
steps: Common face across both views: 2 (on top both times).
Faces seen adjacent to 2 in Position 1: 3 and 4.
Faces seen adjacent to 2 in Position 2: 5 and 6.
All adjacent faces seen so far: 3, 4, 5, 6 — four distinct faces.
Out of the six faces (1-6), only face 1 has never appeared adjacent to 2.

trickPractice.trick: The face NEVER seen next to it, across all views, is the opposite
trickPractice.intro: Combine adjacency information from every view given — the single leftover face is always the answer.

questions.q: Die faces 1-6. Position 1: top=4, sides 1,2. Position 2: top=4, sides 3,5. Which face is opposite 4?

commonMistakes.mistake: Applying the sum-to-7 shortcut to a die with non-standard labels (letters, colors, or an unusual number arrangement) where it doesn't apply.
commonMistakes.fix: Only use sum-to-7 for confirmed standard 1-6 dice. For anything else, use the two-view adjacency method instead.

commonMistakes.mistake: Only checking adjacency from ONE of the two given views, missing faces revealed in the second view.
commonMistakes.fix: Always combine adjacency information from EVERY view given before concluding — a face might only be revealed as adjacent in the second picture.

commonMistakes.mistake: Mistakenly treating a face seen next to the target face (adjacent) as if it were the opposite face.
commonMistakes.fix: Remember: faces touching an edge are adjacent, never opposite. The opposite face is always the one that never shows up next to it in any view.

revisionCard.summary: Standard numbered dice: opposite faces always sum to 7 (1-6, 2-5, 3-4). For non-standard dice, compare two views sharing a common face — every face seen adjacent to it across both views is ruled out; the one face never seen adjacent is the opposite. Every cube face has exactly 4 adjacent faces and exactly 1 opposite face.

gameMission.title: The Jungle Dice Roll
gameMission.brief: Study two rolls of the jungle animals' magic die and figure out which face is hiding on the opposite side!

realLifeProject: Find a real die at home, roll it twice, note the top and two visible side faces each time, and use the two-view method to confirm the opposite of a chosen face — then check by simply looking at the bottom face.

rememberIt.hook: Standard dice: sum to 7. Otherwise: two views, find the leftover face
rememberIt.unpack: Adjacent faces are ruled out; the one face never seen next to it across all views is opposite.

studentQuestions.q: What if only ONE view of a non-standard die is given?
studentQuestions.a: With just one view, you usually can't determine the exact opposite face uniquely — you need a second view (or other given clues) revealing more adjacency information to narrow it down to exactly one leftover face.

studentQuestions.q: Does this two-view method work for finding ADJACENT faces too, not just opposite ones?
studentQuestions.a: Yes — any face you directly see next to the target face in any view is confirmed adjacent to it immediately; you don't need to wait for a second view for that part.
